input.title: Apple and NVIDIA: revenue growth, net margin, and main filing risks
input.content:
# Summary
Apple and NVIDIA both posted revenue growth and strong net margins in their latest annual periods, but NVIDIA’s growth and profitability were materially higher than Apple’s per the stored annual financials. The companies also describe different main risk themes in their filings: Apple emphasizes competition, product transitions, regulation, supply chain constraints, and demand management, while NVIDIA emphasizes rapid product transitions, demand forecasting, competition, and customer/channel concentration.[1629][1659][1672][1634][1857][1859][1706][1894]

# Comparison
| Company | Metric | Latest period_end | Value |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Apple | Revenue growth | 2025-09-27 | 6.43% per the stored FY2025 financials |
| NVIDIA | Revenue growth | 2026-01-25 | 65.47% per the stored FY2026 financials |
| Apple | Net margin | 2025-09-27 | 26.92% per the stored FY2025 financials |
| NVIDIA | Net margin | 2026-01-25 | 55.60% per the stored FY2026 financials |

The latest period_end dates are 120 days apart, so the latest values do not cover the same calendar period.

## Apple
Apple’s latest annual revenue growth was 6.43% for the period ending 2025-09-27, per the stored FY2025 financials. Apple’s latest annual net margin was 26.92% for the period ending 2025-09-27, per the stored FY2025 financials.

Apple says it operates in highly volatile and competitive markets and must continually introduce new products, services, and technologies, while stimulating demand and managing transitions to new and upgraded offerings.[1629] Apple also says success depends on recruiting and retaining skilled personnel, timely development and market acceptance of new products, and managing risks around new technologies, production ramp-up, third-party integrations, and inventory levels.[1629]

Apple’s filing also highlights legal and regulatory risk. It says new and changing laws, regulations, executive orders, directives, and enforcement priorities can raise costs, limit offerings, force design changes, affect customer demand, and require business or supply-chain changes.[1659] It further notes that these risks expand as Apple enters specialized applications and expands AI-related technologies.[1659]

Supply chain risk is another major theme. Apple says changes to its supply chain require time and resources, and that it depends on obtaining components in sufficient quantities on commercially reasonable terms.[1634] It adds that some components come from single or limited sources, creating significant supply and pricing risks, and that shortages or commodity price fluctuations could materially adversely affect the business.[1634]

Apple also states that its gross margins and net sales can be pressured by pricing competition, supply shortages, higher component and manufacturing costs, mix shifts, tariffs, foreign exchange, inflation, and new products with lower margins.[1672]

## NVIDIA
NVIDIA’s latest annual revenue growth was 65.47% for the period ending 2026-01-25, per the stored FY2026 financials. NVIDIA’s latest annual net margin was 55.60% for the period ending 2026-01-25, per the stored FY2026 financials.

NVIDIA’s filings emphasize product transitions and revenue volatility. The company says it often ships new and prior architecture products at the same time, that transitions across Data Center, Gaming, Professional Visualization, and Automotive can be complex, and that more frequent transitions may magnify supply-and-demand challenges and create revenue volatility.[1857] It also says customers may delay adoption of new architectures, which can affect the timing of revenue.[1857]

NVIDIA further states that customer demand estimates can be wrong, creating volatility in revenue or supply levels, and that it may be difficult to estimate the impact of accelerated computing and AI models on reported revenue or forecast demand.[1859]

Competition is also a key risk. NVIDIA says rivals may have more financial, sales, marketing, and distribution resources, may transition products faster, may secure scarce foundry capacity and input materials, and could take market share or prevent NVIDIA from doing so.[1706] The filing also notes that some customers have in-house capabilities and can develop alternatives.[1706]

NVIDIA’s filing highlights customer and channel concentration. It says it generates a significant amount of revenue from a limited number of indirect customers, some individually representing 10% or more of revenue, and that the loss of a large customer, reduced purchases, trade restrictions, or collection issues could harm results.[1894]

# Main risks from the filings
- **Apple:** competition and product-transition execution, regulatory and legal changes, supply-chain constraints, and margin pressure from pricing, costs, tariffs, and mix shifts.[1629][1659][1672][1634]
- **NVIDIA:** product-transition complexity, demand forecasting error, competitive pressure, and customer/channel concentration.[1857][1859][1706][1894]

# Data and limits
This report uses the stored annual financials for revenue growth and net margin, and the stored 10-K risk factor passages for qualitative risks. Apple and NVIDIA do not share the same fiscal year-end, so their latest annual figures are from different calendar periods: Apple 2025-09-27 and NVIDIA 2026-01-25.

The risk-factor passages are selected excerpts, not the full filings, and only cover the filing text available in the stored search results. If a risk is not mentioned above, it is not necessarily absent; it was simply not found in the passages returned in this run.
